A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CVFM research work. All 31 pages of v3 and 35 pages of v4, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original CVFM evaluations on synthetic conditional mappings, MNIST–FashionMNIST transfer and materials dynamics.

after.justification: v4 retains these original evaluations and adds quantitative and visual comparisons of predicted materials distributions.

M1.justification: The written kernel formula changes from an unsquared conditioning difference to a squared Euclidean mismatch. Algorithm 2 also replaces bridge sampling variances σ²t(1−t) with constant σ² while retaining bridge drift/score formulas, creating an inconsistency. The core framework persists; Algorithm 3 mainly documents the existing materials application.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three synthetic mappings, MNIST–FashionMNIST transfer and 10,000 materials trajectories spanning 100 frames. The new mobility-bin analysis uses the retained test data and task.

E2.justification: Corresponding synthetic, image-transfer and materials comparisons retain their baseline sets, including both T-COT-SFM variants. Table 3 uses CVSFM/COT-SFM variants already evaluated in the materials study; newly cited conditional-OT works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Reported materials settings change from batch size 256, σ_y=0.01 and η=10 to effective batch size 1024, σ_y=0.1 and η=100. v4 also introduces time-averaged Wasserstein-2 evaluation within three mobility bins. The retained Table 2 numbers do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 3 and revised Figure 4 add an analysis of materials distribution fidelity across mobility bins and time, supplementing trajectory-error evaluation. Existing kernel ablations, sensitivity analyses, error distributions and sample-trajectory analyses remain.

E5.justification: Five-seed reporting for the synthetic results and objective-variance analysis is unchanged, as are existing mean/standard-deviation reporting practices. Table 3 supplies point estimates without introducing new run counts, confidence intervals or statistical tests.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1 and 2 and both existing appendix tables are unchanged. New Table 3 reports CVSFM errors of 0.637/0.628/0.646 versus COT-SFM's 0.674/0.608/0.690 across three bins, favoring CVSFM in two bins. Entropic-variant results and materials distribution plots are also added.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 substantially expands the central loss-equivalence argument: v3 invokes α→1 as η→∞, whereas v4 adds near-matching and smoothness assumptions and a Taylor argument for first-order agreement at finite mismatch. The exact statement of Theorem 3.2 remains unreconciled with this qualification. Appendix C also replaces the schematic spinodal equation with explicit mobility and free-energy definitions.

C1.justification: The core claims remain learning continuously conditioned dynamics from unpaired observations through conditional flows, OT and kernel weighting, with a Schrödinger-bridge extension and improved convergence. Abstract and conclusion revisions retain this contribution scope.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly discusses approximate kernel-weighted loss equivalence and leaves more precise kernel analysis to future work. It also explains that only one trajectory is available per complete conditioning vector, motivating mobility-bin evaluation, and interprets the new plots as evidence of recovering distribution width and shape.

D1.justification: v4 substantially expands documentation of toy-data sampling, PCA fitted on training data, phase-field parameters and initialization, and sampling adjacent time marginals with time interpolation in Algorithm 3. These details describe retained experiments. The previously reported 7,800-step materials training budget disappears; hardware and code-access information remain.

R1.justification: v4 adds Tabak et al. and Baptista et al. to its conditional-OT positioning, including discussion of high-dimensional scalability. Additional citations support phase-field simulation, stochastic microstructure representations and LSTM; the principal relationships to existing flow-matching methods remain.

P1.justification: Substantial explanatory rewriting clarifies unpaired sampling and expands experimental construction and materials background. The background appendices exchange order, and experimental details now precede supplementary results. These changes substantially reorganize and explain existing content while retaining the main section outline.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is redesigned with materials marginal-comparison panels; its former error plots remain in Appendix E.7. Table 3 and Algorithm 3 are added, pseudocode is expanded, and several tables and plots move. Other figure images are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added materials distribution checks and clearer sampling and temporal-training documentation strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. The gain is limited by evaluation that pools over two conditioning variables, the unreconciled exact-versus-approximate loss claims, and the newly inconsistent sampling variances in Algorithm 2.
